clue.text: Having botched raid, cop intended to take off

definitions.note: adjectival phrase: meant as a send-up or mimicry

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A policeman flees the scene after a raid goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like a getaway but means imitate; 'botched' rearranges RAID and COP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something parodic is designed to mimic and mock its original, which is what a take-off does.

clue.text: One about to be enrolled in college course

indicators.note: enrolled as a student, so the pieces go inside the word for college

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of British college
I is the Roman numeral one
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A student is about to join a college course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a course of action, not a college class; POLY was a British polytechnic college.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy is a planned course of action adopted by a body.

clue.text: Upset about drug? Say nothing for a change

indicators.note: the word for upset goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to ruffle is to upset or disturb
E is short for ecstasy
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A drug scandal causes upset, and a cabinet-style call for silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the definition but is wordplay; the definition is 'a change', with 'for' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reshuffle is a reorganisation, typically of government posts, so a change of personnel.

clue.text: Duke replaces leader in boat — he might sound like John Wayne

definitions.text: he might sound like John Wayne

indicators.note: the duke's letter takes the place of the first letter of the boat

parts.note: a trawler is a fishing boat

explanation.surface: John Wayne, nicknamed the Duke, takes charge of a fishing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wayne's nickname was 'the Duke', but here Duke is simply D.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wayne was known for his slow, drawn-out way of speaking, the mark of someone who drawls.

clue.text: TV technicians arrived with noodles

indicators.note: joins one piece directly to the next

parts.note: came means arrived
ramen are Japanese noodles

explanation.surface: The TV crew showed up with a takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Camera operators on a television crew are the technicians who film the shots.

clue.text: Reason for guttering somewhere in Ireland?

definitions.meaning: a candle gutters, flickering and dripping, when its wick burns down low
a county on Ireland's east coast, south of Dublin

explanation.surface: A question about why a candle flickers, posed as a place quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the county name into WICK LOW and it explains a sputtering candle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicklow is an Irish county and town; read as two words it describes a burnt-down candle wick.

clue.text: Nest builders used to be extremely pestiferous

parts.note: was means used to be

indicators.note: takes the extreme letters, first and last, of the following word

explanation.surface: Whatever built this nest was a real pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasps build papery nests, so the insects are nest builders.

clue.text: Cause of psychic conflict not easily understood

definitions.meaning: in psychology, a group of repressed ideas causing abnormal behaviour or anxiety

explanation.surface: A puzzling source of mental turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A complex in psychology is a cluster of repressed feelings; as an adjective it means intricate.

clue.text: Cause of memory loss in little theatre

indicators.note: the letters are found within the next two words

explanation.surface: Forgetting one's lines in a small theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking from the mythical river Lethe made the dead forget their earthly lives.

clue.text: Flap under source of water for flush

indicators.note: in a down clue the flap piece sits below the water piece

parts.note: a well is a source of water
a to-do is a flap, a fuss

explanation.surface: A panic about a toilet cistern beneath a water tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' looks like plumbing but means having plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flush means having plenty of money, so wealthy or prosperous.

clue.text: Girl hugging tree, first in Adriatic resort

indicators.note: to hug something is to wrap around it, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: a lass is a girl
the palm is a tree

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A girl embraces a tree at a seaside resort on the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adriatic' tempts a solver to think of Italy or Croatia, but it only gives its first letter; the resort is in the Canaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Palmas, on Gran Canaria, is a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: For example, Iron Maiden and others

definitions.text: For example, Iron Maiden and others

parts.words: For example, Iron Maiden and others
parts.note: iron is an element of this kind, and Iron Maiden is a heavy band of this musical genre, as are its peers

explanation.surface: A list of heavy rock bands, starting with Iron Maiden.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Iron' alone, it is a chemical element; read whole, it is the band's musical genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is a metallic element, and Iron Maiden plays heavy music of the genre named after such elements.

clue.text: Yarn we hear causing pain

indicators.note: signals that the word for yarn is to be spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: crewel is a thin worsted yarn used in embroidery

explanation.surface: A tale whose telling is painful to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a story, but it is embroidery wool, CREWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel treatment inflicts suffering, so the adjective means pain-inflicting.

clue.text: Recovering readily, one boy coming back in break

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the word for a break

parts.note: a rest is a break

indicators.note: the boy and the one are read backwards, returning on themselves

parts.note: Neil is a boy's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boy bounces back during a pause from his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns the boy and the one round to give ILIEN, which 'in' places inside the break.
explanation.definitionFit: A resilient person or material bounces back quickly after pressure or setback.

clue.text: Author crossing city, crossing in a paddy

parts.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing
a paddy is a fit of temper, so someone in one is mad, angry
Oxford is an English university city

explanation.surface: A writer storms across town in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's name itself means a crossing, so the first 'crossing' also points at OXFORD; FORD, MAD and OXFORD join.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford Madox Ford wrote The Good Soldier and the Parade's End novels.

clue.text: Ladies etc dressed in fine garments

indicators.note: dressed means arranged or prepared, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Women and others wearing their finest clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicates are flimsy items of clothing, such as lingerie, needing gentle washing.

clue.text: Spare juice for master

parts.note: over means left over, spare
juice is slang for electric power

explanation.surface: A request for extra energy for the master of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To master an opponent is to overcome or subdue them, which is to overpower.

clue.text: Indecent sailor beginning to rant in dialect mostly

indicators.note: the sailor and the letter go inside the shortened dialect
the dialect loses its last letter

parts.note: Scouse is the dialect of Liverpool
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A sailor rants rudely in a thick regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse is the accent of Liverpool; 'mostly' cuts its last letter, leaving SCOUS, which 'in' wraps round the sailor and the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabrous can mean salacious or rude, as of a joke or story, so indecent.

clue.text: Custard given fancy name? Sacrilege!

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborate or rearranged, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is scandalised that plain custard has been given a pretentious name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges NAME and SACRILEGE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème anglaise is the French term for a thin pouring custard.

clue.text: Heart of French cat, say

indicators.note: takes the central letters of the following word

parts.note: the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: Introducing a French cat, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the definition; the middle of FRENCH is EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to pronounce or state, so to utter words.

clue.text: Order routine before delivery

indicators.note: used as a verb: arrange the letters of the next word into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Following the usual procedure before a parcel arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' is childbirth, not a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: In utero means in the womb, so the state of a baby before birth.

clue.text: See how far you can go without unknown god

indicators.note: the unknown letter is taken out of the phrase

parts.words: See how far you can go
parts.note: to try it on is to test how much one can get away with
y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A challenge to push one's luck without knowing a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton is a Greek sea deity, the son of Poseidon.

clue.text: See piece next to king? Not hard

indicators.note: places the chess piece beside what follows

parts.note: the bishop is a chess piece

indicators.note: the word for hard is left out of the king's name

parts.note: Richard is the name of several English kings
taken as the word itself, removed

explanation.surface: A chess problem: find the piece standing beside the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is the definition, a bishop's area; 'Not hard' removes HARD from RICHARD, leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district or office of a bishop, which is a bishopric.

clue.text: Proceed without interruption, say, in appeal

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for appeal

parts.note: to sue is to appeal or plead
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A court appeal carries on without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to move smoothly from one thing to the next without pause.

clue.text: Sultanate supporting right type

indicators.note: in a down clue the sultanate sits under, holding up, the letter above

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A sultanate backs the right sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' means a typeface, not a kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the upright typeface used for ordinary print, as opposed to italic.

clue.text: Superior meal but no starter

indicators.note: the meal is served without its first letter, as without a first course

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A fine dinner, though one without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starter' punningly removes the first letter S from SUPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher in rank or status, as in the upper class.

clue.text: Bach provided notes for this publication

definitions.meaning: J. S. Bach wrote much music for this keyboard instrument
a newspaper or periodical serving as the mouthpiece of a party or body

explanation.surface: A composer's score was printed in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' are musical, not written comments.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is the instrument of Bach's toccatas; an organ is also an official journal.

clue.text: Nous when involved with metro

indicators.note: involved means entangled, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Common sense is needed when riding the underground railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nous' is British slang for common sense; 'involved' rearranges WITH and METRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother wit is native common sense, the same practical intelligence as nous.

clue.text: Lustre enveloping empty bottle —- moonshine here?

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap round, so the word for lustre surrounds the other piece

parts.note: sheen is a lustre or shine

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A gleaming empty bottle prompts a question about where illicit liquor is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den in Ireland or Scotland; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal home-distilled spirit would be sold at an unlicensed drinking house of this kind.

clue.text: Hanger-on in Braemar fled after games? Not quite

indicators.note: the fled piece comes after the games piece
the word for games is cut just short of its end

parts.note: sport means games collectively
ran means fled

explanation.surface: Someone flees Braemar after the Highland games.
explanation.walkthrough: Braemar is a Scottish village famous for its Highland Games; a sporran hangs from a kilt belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the pouch that hangs in front of a kilt, worn in Scottish places like Braemar.
